elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (positioned between 9.3 and 9.5): "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor." Section 2.1 was conformed from "without reduction or termination rights" to "without reduction rights but subject to Section 9.4," so the take-or-pay sentence no longer contradicts the new right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — 30 days, in writing, no additional conditions or Vendor consent.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Relied-on Section 10.2 says only "Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination." A refund covering the post-termination period is not an express pro-rata refund, and the retained wording is limited to prepaid *recurring* Fees, so prepaid non-recurring amounts within the defined term "Fees" (e.g., prepaid professional services or usage fees) are excluded. The new convenience clause itself contains no refund mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted second sentence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Sections 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only cause/insolvency triggers, so nothing retained contradicts this.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on "thirty days' prior written notice," which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to us, but literally not this element).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee or exit charge appears anywhere in the redlined text, and the Section 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is now expressly "subject to Section 9.4," so it cannot operate as a residual exit penalty after a convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term," and no Vendor convenience right exists elsewhere (9.1–9.3 are cause-based; 27.3 is force majeure).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor holds no convenience termination right at all under the redlined Section 9, so no notice period is required of it.

reasons: Not position-complete. The preferred level fails on the refund element: Section 10.2's retained "refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination" is a post-termination-period refund, not an express pro-rata refund, and it is narrowed to *recurring* Fees so prepaid professional services/usage Fees are not returned. Repair in operative language by adding to the new convenience clause: "...in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination," or by amending 10.2 to read "refund on a pro-rata basis all prepaid Fees".

The fallback level is not independently complete either (30 days' notice is outside the 60–90 day band), so the finding cannot rest on the fallback as an alternative; the fix must be made at the preferred level.

Minimality holds: only two edits were made — the concise insertion of the convenience right plus the Vendor no-convenience sentence (both mapped to preferred elements), and the narrow conforming change to Section 2.1 that deletes only the words "or termination" while preserving the Customer-adverse-but-retained "without reduction rights." The model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted, and no survival tail, expense, or procedural extras were added.

Intent is preserved: cause, insolvency, Security-Incident, multi-Order-Form and remedy-cumulation mechanics in 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 survive unchanged, and 10.2 is untouched. One drafting point to confirm on execution: the inserted paragraph must be numbered "9.4" (it sits between 9.3 and 9.5) so that the new cross-reference in Section 2.1 ("subject to Section 9.4") resolves; as rendered the insertion carries no section number while every neighbouring provision does.

Classification as a deviation is correct: before the redline there was no Customer convenience right in a three-year committed term, with Section 2.1 expressly denying termination rights — walk-away territory.
